angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 578,127 km at 5.11 pc = 1.51 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 195.5674 +/- 0.1964 mas (same row, RUWE 3.27): 5.11 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.831 +/- 0.0044 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 702A: radius in solar radii, 0.831 +/- 0.0044, from this work (CHARA) (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112): 578,127 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.846 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 702A: mass 0.846 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5407 +/- 52 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 702A: effective temperature in K, 5407 +/- 52, from this work (CHARA) (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 702A: effective temperature in K, 5407 +/- 52, from this work (CHARA) (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/757/2/112)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-702-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.526, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
